sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: FINDING COMMON GROUND 3 3.1 The Greatest of All Sameeksha is building her new house.
sections.source_evidence: FINDING COMMON GROUND 3 3.1 The Greatest of All Sameeksha is building her new house.

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: The main room of the house is 12 ft by 16 ft.
sections.source_evidence: The main room of the house is 12 ft by 16 ft.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: She feels that the room would look nice if the floor is covered with square tiles of the same size.
sections.source_evidence: She feels that the room would look nice if the floor is covered with square tiles of the same size.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: She also wants to use as few tiles as possible, and for the length of the tile to be a whole number of feet.
sections.source_evidence: She also wants to use as few tiles as possible, and for the length of the tile to be a whole number of feet.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: Let us explore how to find the largest square tile that can be used.
sections.source_evidence: Let us explore how to find the largest square tile that can be used.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: The breadth of the room is 12 ft and the length is 16 ft.
sections.source_evidence: The breadth of the room is 12 ft and the length is 16 ft.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: For the tiles to fit the breadth of the room exactly, the side of the tile should be a factor of 12.
sections.source_evidence: For the tiles to fit the breadth of the room exactly, the side of the tile should be a factor of 12.

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Similarly, for the tiles to fit the length of the room exactly, the side should be a factor of 16.
sections.source_evidence: Similarly, for the tiles to fit the length of the room exactly, the side should be a factor of 16.

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: So the side of the tile should be a factor of both 12 and 16.
sections.source_evidence: So the side of the tile should be a factor of both 12 and 16.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: What are the common factors of 12 and 16?
sections.source_evidence: What are the common factors of 12 and 16?

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
sections.source_evidence: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: So, the square tiles can have sides 1 ft, 2 ft, and 4 ft.
sections.source_evidence: So, the square tiles can have sides 1 ft, 2 ft, and 4 ft.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: Among these, she should use the largest sized square tile.
sections.source_evidence: Among these, she should use the largest sized square tile.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Therefore, she needs tiles of size 4 ft.
sections.source_evidence: Therefore, she needs tiles of size 4 ft.

sections.heading: Learning Point 15
sections.content: Ganita Prakash | Grade 7 | Part-II How many tiles of this size should she purchase?
sections.source_evidence: Ganita Prakash | Grade 7 | Part-II How many tiles of this size should she purchase?

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: What if Sameeksha did not insist on the length of the tile to be a whole number of feet and the length could be a fractional number of feet?
sections.source_evidence: What if Sameeksha did not insist on the length of the tile to be a whole number of feet and the length could be a fractional number of feet?

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: The Highest Common Factor (HCF) of two or more numbers, is the highest (or greatest) of their common factors.
sections.source_evidence: The Highest Common Factor (HCF) of two or more numbers, is the highest (or greatest) of their common factors.

sections.heading: Learning Point 18
sections.content: It is also known as the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD).
sections.source_evidence: It is also known as the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD).

sections.heading: Learning Point 19
sections.content: In the previous problem, 4 is the HCF of 12 and 16.
sections.source_evidence: In the previous problem, 4 is the HCF of 12 and 16.

sections.heading: Learning Point 20
sections.content: We can draw rough diagrams like the one shown on the previous page to visualise the given scenario.
